component.name: CardHorizontal
component.description: A horizontal course card (thumbnail-left layout) with an 80×80px square thumbnail and a content column: the title and optional ProgressBar (stack xs), then a metadata row (Inline gap sm) at stack sm. The metadata row renders author · duration (a 4px separator dot only between those two, drawn by the component) and the certified badge (no separator; its icon already sets it apart). Two usages: started courses (default variant, progress, duration, optional certified) and footer promotion (inverted variant, author, duration). For vertical image-top course cards use CardVertical; for generic surface containers use Card.

when: Listing started or saved courses in the User Settings page
Displaying course recommendations in a footer or sidebar with an inverted dark background

patterns.name: started-courses-list
patterns.description: Courses the learner has started: a vertical Stack of CardHorizontal items with progress, duration and optional certified. No author.
patterns.tree: Stack(gap=sm) > [CardHorizontal(title, progress=65, duration, certified), CardHorizontal(title, progress=20, duration), ...]

patterns.name: footer-recommendations
patterns.description: Promotional, not-started items in the dark footer: inverted variant with author and duration, no progress. The Box provides the inverted background color; no theme switch is needed — both parent and cards stay in the light theme.

patterns.name: certified-badge
patterns.description: The Icon+Text 'Certified' badge in the metadata row is not exclusive to this component's internal layout — reuse the same composition wherever a certified badge appears outside a Card (e.g. a page's course-detail metadata row). Icon gets its color from a `.badge svg { color: var(--ds-color-icon-subtle); }` rule in a co-located CSS Module, targeting the ancestor per the Icon color rule (.claude/rules/components.md) — never an inline `style={{ color }}` on the wrapping element. On an inverted surface, override it with color.icon.inverted.default.

antiPatterns.reason: Creates doubled surface depth that loses hierarchy meaning.
antiPatterns.alternative: Place CardHorizontal directly in a Stack or Inline layout.

antiPatterns.scenario: Mixing CardHorizontal and CardVertical in the same list
antiPatterns.reason: Inconsistent layout direction breaks visual rhythm in a list or grid.
antiPatterns.alternative: Pick one orientation for a given context: CardVertical for catalog grids, CardHorizontal for compact lists and footers.

antiPatterns.scenario: Using CardHorizontal for non-course content (e.g., user profile, article)
antiPatterns.reason: The fixed 80×80 thumbnail and metadata row are designed for course items.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use Card with a custom inner layout for other content types.

antiPatterns.scenario: Placing CardHorizontal alongside Card or CardVertical in the same visual group
antiPatterns.reason: The three card variants have different aspect ratios, thumbnail shapes, and content structures. Mixing them in the same row or list breaks visual rhythm.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use one card variant consistently per section. CardHorizontal works best in vertical lists (e.g. search results, inverted footer sections); CardVertical in horizontal carousels.

antiPatterns.reason: ProgressBar has no inverted treatment: its track (background.overlay-subtle) and fill are not contrast-checked against color.background.container.inverted.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use progress only on the default variant; inverted footer cards show duration and certified only.

antiPatterns.scenario: Colouring the inverted variant with an inline style or a colour rule on the card root
antiPatterns.reason: Heading and Text own their colour through the color prop; inline colour bypasses the typography API and the no-inline-colour rule.
antiPatterns.alternative: Pass Heading color="inverted" and Text color="inverted-subtle"; only the badge icon needs a CSS Module override (.inverted .badge svg).

antiPatterns.scenario: Packing the author (or a topic) into duration, e.g. duration="Jon Kabat-Zinn · 2 hours, 15min"
antiPatterns.reason: Each prop holds one kind of data. A merged string hides the author from consumers, agents and Figma (Author/Duration are separate properties), and hand-typed separators drift from the component's separator dot.
antiPatterns.alternative: Pass author="Jon Kabat-Zinn" duration="2 hours, 15min"; the component draws the separator.

antiPatterns.scenario: Adding a separator before the certified badge, or typing "·" in any metadata string
antiPatterns.reason: The separator sits only between author and duration; the badge icon already separates Certified. Separators are rendered by the component (aria-hidden), never typed.
antiPatterns.alternative: Pass the plain values; let CardHorizontal decide where separators go.

antiPatterns.scenario: Placing CardHorizontal in a section whose heading is not an h2 (e.g. directly under the page h1, or inside an h3 subsection)
antiPatterns.reason: The title always renders as an h3 (there is no heading-level prop), so any parent heading other than h2 skips or inverts a level in the document outline.
antiPatterns.alternative: Put CardHorizontal lists inside a section headed by an h2. If a layout needs another level, raise it as a component change (a titleAs prop) instead of wrapping or restyling the card.

antiPatterns.scenario: Passing long course titles and expecting them to wrap
antiPatterns.reason: The title is a single line with an ellipsis. Sighted users lose the truncated text (screen readers still get the full title), and the risk grows at 200% zoom.
antiPatterns.alternative: Keep titles short enough to fit the list width. Use CardVertical when titles are long.

purpose.default: Standard light-theme context. Text uses default and subtle color tokens.
purpose.inverted: Inverted-background context within the light theme (e.g. the dark footer section). Switches the title to Heading color=inverted, metadata to Text color=inverted-subtle, and the badge icon to color.icon.inverted.default. The parent container must supply the dark background via color.background.container.inverted — do NOT use data-theme='dark'. Figma: Variant=inverted.

states.description: Static display card — no interactive states.

ariaAttributes: role=article on the root, aria-labelledby → the title Heading's id (useId); role, children and aria-labelledby are omitted from the props type so consumers cannot override them
thumbnailAlt (pass a meaningful description of the course image, or empty string if the title already provides context)
Progress: ProgressBar aria-labelledby → the title id (no duplicated '<title> progress' string)
